text: The Patriots face a significant challenge heading into their Week 2 home opener against the Steelers on Sunday at 1 PM ET, with wide receiver A.J. Brown heading to injured reserve after suffering a high ankle sprain in the season opener—a loss that will sideline him for at least four weeks and force the offensive weapons around Drake Maye to step up considerably against Pittsburgh's defense. While the offense absorbs that blow, quarterback Maye has already demonstrated his character off the field, joining his wife Ann Michael in purchasing Amazon classroom wish lists for more than 50 teachers and support specialists at Alfred Lima Sr. Elementary School in Providence, Rhode Island, showcasing the kind of community engagement that matters in New England. Head Coach Mike Vrabel addressed the team's readiness in his Wednesday press conference, and the full injury report has been released for both squads ahead of Sunday's matchup. Additionally, Patriots owner Robert Kraft made clear the organization's values extend beyond football, announcing he had Macklemore removed as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's upcoming Gillette Stadium shows, citing "a history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community."
